what: Narrative devices: the one idea a film is built on, laid over any product so the story is not the default launch arc. Used by scripts/story.mjs (pick samples three that differ on the axes; check scores a pitch against the cliche arc). Schema: taxonomy/devices-SCHEMA.md.

container.name: Borrowed container
container.what: Hijack a form the audience already reads fluently (a search box, a receipt, a weather report) and misuse its grammar.

camera.name: Camera / space
camera.what: One camera or framing rule carries the whole film (no cuts, one zoom, a locked frame, a split).

time.name: Time
time.what: One rule about time (compressed, reversed, looped, real time, from the future) shapes the story.

rhetoric.name: Structural / rhetorical
rhetoric.what: A shape of argument (misdirect, list that breaks, question chain) with a built-in turn.

character.name: Character
character.what: Who tells it or whom it follows is the idea (the product, the villain, the skeptic, the least likely witness).

metaphor.name: Metaphor / world
metaphor.what: One metaphor or invented world, rendered physically and pushed as far as it goes.

constraint.name: Constraint / stunt
constraint.what: A strict self-imposed rule (five seconds, only words, one shape, made from the product's output).

turn.what: The kind of turn at 60-75% of the film.

visual_world.what: The visual register the film lives in.

cliche.what: The default launch arc every AI-made video falls into: a sales deck built outward from the feature list, with no turn. A pitch that reuses 4+ of these beats in this order, or lists three features back to back, fails check's gate G1.
cliche.arc: hook stat or question -> problem montage -> "Introducing <product>" logo reveal -> feature 1 -> feature 2 -> feature 3 -> social proof -> CTA

beats.name: Hook stat or question
beats.what: Opens on a statistic or a rhetorical question ("Drowning in X?", "73% of teams...").

beats.name: Problem montage
beats.what: Quick cuts of people or screens suffering the problem.

beats.name: "Introducing <product>" reveal
beats.what: The product name or logo arrives as the answer.

beats.name: Feature 1
beats.what: First feature card or UI demo.

beats.name: Feature 2
beats.what: Second feature card or UI demo.

beats.name: Feature 3
beats.what: Third feature card or UI demo.

overused_patterns.name: Chaos to calm
overused_patterns.what: A messy montage resolves into a clean UI (a subtype of before/after).

overused_patterns.name: Typing into a glowing prompt box
overused_patterns.what: The default opener for AI products: a caret blinks in a glowing input, a prompt types itself.

overused_patterns.name: Friendly blob mascot
overused_patterns.what: A soft rounded character stands in for the product.

overused_patterns.name: Hyperlapse day
overused_patterns.what: Dawn to dusk at 100x with the product in every micro-moment.

visuals.name: Dashboard floating in a void at a 30-degree tilt
The glowing globe / network of arcs

devices.name: The Search / Query Log
devices.what: The whole story is told through what one person types into a box, one query at a time.

beats.name: Innocent query
beats.purpose: Sets the person and the stakes in a few typed words.

beats.name: Escalating queries
beats.purpose: Each query reveals more of a life; the gaps carry the emotion.

beats.name: Turning-point query
beats.purpose: One query changes the story's direction (the turn).

beats.name: Resolution query
beats.purpose: A quiet, often funny query shows the new life.

beats.name: Name
beats.purpose: The product name in the same box, or as the last result.

devices.example: A travel app: "cheap flights lisbon" -> "lisbon alone safe" -> "portuguese for 'is this seat taken'" -> "lisbon apartment long term".
pitfalls: A gimmick with no emotional arc
Too many queries; five to eight is plenty
Typing too fast to read (at least 0.3 s per word)
The default AI glowing prompt box: use the product's real input, not a generic one

build.note: Typing animation, a caret, hard cuts between queries; the product's real input field if it has one.

devices.name: The Receipt
devices.what: The film is one long receipt printing; its line items tell the story and the total is the punchline.

beats.name: Header
beats.purpose: The store name is the setting ("YOUR 2025", "MONDAY STANDUP").

beats.name: Line items
beats.purpose: Items escalate from literal to emotional, each with a price.

beats.name: Subtotal
beats.purpose: The turn: a line that reframes the cost.

beats.name: Total
beats.purpose: The payoff line, in the receipt's own grammar.

beats.name: Footer
beats.purpose: "THANK YOU, COME AGAIN" becomes the sign-off.

devices.example: A meeting-notes app: "STANDUP x 212 ... 53 HRS", "'CAN YOU SEE MY SCREEN' x 94", subtotal "MEETINGS THAT COULD BE A NOTE: 61%", total "YOU GET BACK: FRIDAYS".
pitfalls: A monotone scroll with no turn line
Generic jokes; every item must be specific
Invented numbers: every figure must be real or clearly playful

build.note: A monospace scroll on a paper texture, a tear at the end.

devices.name: The Chat Conversation
devices.what: The story plays out in a messaging thread, typing dots and all.

beats.name: Opening message
beats.purpose: Who's talking and what they want.

beats.name: Escalation
beats.purpose: A misunderstanding or a pile-up of messages.

beats.name: The reply
beats.purpose: The message that changes everything (the turn).

beats.name: Last message
beats.purpose: The sign-off doubles as the call to action.

devices.example: A code-review tool: a junior dev and a senior in DMs at 11 pm, "quick q", a 400-line diff, three dots... "approved. go to bed."
pitfalls: Everyone does fake iMessage: subvert the sender, the platform or the voice
Reading load: keep messages to a few words
A chatbot thread for an AI product is the most generic option there is

build.note: Bubbles, typing dots, timestamps.

devices.name: The Weather Report
devices.what: A broadcast forecast where the weather is the problem domain, with fronts, warnings and an outlook.

beats.name: Fronts on the map
beats.purpose: The problem as weather systems moving in.

beats.name: Seven-day outlook
beats.purpose: The new normal, as icons; the sign-off.

devices.example: An uptime monitor: "a cold front of 502s moving over us-east, a 90% chance of pager by 3 am... but a high-pressure alerting system is pushing through. Outlook: sleep."
pitfalls: The joke fades after 20 s: keep it under 45 s or escalate
Map clutter; one front per beat

build.note: A map, weather icons, lower thirds, a ticker.

devices.name: The Museum Exhibit / Auction
devices.what: The old way presented as artifacts in a gallery (or lots at an auction), with placards.

beats.name: Entrance plaque
beats.purpose: Names the museum: the whole premise in one line.

beats.name: Exhibits
beats.purpose: Two to four artifacts of the old way, each with a witty placard.

beats.name: The empty plinth
beats.purpose: The turn: where the problem used to be.

beats.name: Gift shop / exit
beats.purpose: The call to action in the museum's grammar.

devices.example: A password manager: "The Museum of Forgotten Passwords": the sticky note on a monitor (c. 1995), "Password1!" under glass, and an empty plinth, "Your next reset. Nothing to see here."
pitfalls: Slow: keep each exhibit to 5 s or less
Placards must be witty and legible at speed

build.note: A slow 2.5D dolly past spotlit objects and placards.

devices.name: The Mock Infomercial
devices.what: The 3 am TV sales format, played straight or ironically.

beats.name: Absurd demo
beats.purpose: The product doing its one thing, overplayed.

beats.name: But wait, there's more!
beats.purpose: The turn: a second capability or a self-aware twist.

beats.name: Flashing offer
beats.purpose: Price and URL in the format's loud type.

devices.example: A calendar app: a man in black and white is buried under double-booked meeting invites, "there's GOT to be a better way!", color, one drag and the week untangles.
pitfalls: It is the cliche arc wearing a costume unless it's self-aware
Needs real craft to read as parody, not cheapness

build.note: Without live action, render as an illustrated or type-driven infomercial with a VHS grade.

devices.name: The Recipe
devices.what: The outcome presented as a dish: ingredients, method, timers and plating.

beats.name: Dish name
beats.purpose: The outcome, named like a recipe ("serves 1 team").

beats.name: Method
beats.purpose: Two or three steps with timers.

beats.name: Plating
beats.purpose: The result, beautifully served (the turn if the method has a surprise).

devices.example: A workflow-automation tool: "Monday Report (serves 1 manager). Ingredients: 3 spreadsheets, 1 CRM, 0 interns. Method: connect, let rest overnight, serve at 9 am."
pitfalls: The overhead cooking-video cliche
The method must reveal a real insight, not just list steps

build.note: A top-down flat lay with labels and timers.

devices.name: The Instruction Manual / Flat-pack Guide
devices.what: Wordless assembly diagrams, numbered steps, a stick figure, a parts list.

beats.name: Parts list
beats.purpose: What you need (and the part you no longer need).

beats.name: Numbered steps
beats.purpose: The figure does it in two or three steps.

beats.name: The removed part
beats.purpose: The turn: the frustration part crossed out.

beats.name: Back page
beats.purpose: The name, like a manual's back cover.

devices.example: A deploy tool: parts "1x repo, 1x branch, 0x YAML (discard)"; step 1 the figure pushes; step 2 a URL appears; the warning icon shows a crossed-out pager.
pitfalls: Can read as help docs: commit fully to the visual language
Too many steps

build.note: Line art with SVG stroke draws and numbered callouts.

devices.name: The Changelog as Poetry
devices.what: Release notes performed as verse: every line a real change, with a volta.

beats.name: Version number
beats.purpose: The title, set like a poem's.

beats.name: Stanzas
beats.purpose: Each line a real, specific change.

beats.name: Volta
beats.purpose: The turn: why it matters, in one line.

devices.example: An editor: "v4 / We taught undo to remember yesterday. / We made search forgive a typo. / We removed a setting nobody found. / We gave you back the afternoon."
pitfalls: Pretentious if the changes are trivial
Every line must be a real change from the actual release notes

build.note: Kinetic type, line by line, with real UI inserts for two lines at most.

devices.name: The Silent Film with Intertitles
devices.what: 1920s title-card storytelling: melodrama, piano, iris wipes.

beats.name: Card: our hero
beats.purpose: Sets the character in the format's voice.

devices.example: A backup app: our heroine's laptop is tied to the tracks by the dastardly Spilled Coffee; card "But lo!"; the files are already safe.
pitfalls: The style is the joke, so the story still needs a real turn
Card reading time

build.note: Grain, vignette, iris wipes, card typography; illustrated or silhouette action.

devices.name: The Nature Documentary
devices.what: A hushed wildlife narrator observes users (or data) in their habitat.

beats.name: Habitat
beats.purpose: The establishing shot, the narrator's voice.

beats.name: An adaptation
beats.purpose: The turn: a new behavior (the product).

devices.example: A team chat app: "Here, in the open-plan office, the Project Manager performs the ancient ritual of the reply-all... but look: a new behavior."
pitfalls: The voice carries it: needs good VO or type-as-VO
Well-worn in comedy; find a specific behavior

build.note: An illustrated or diorama habitat, observational framing, lower-third species labels.

devices.name: The Sports Broadcast / Play-by-play
devices.what: Commentators call a mundane task as a big game, with replays, a telestrator and stat overlays.

beats.name: Slow-mo replay
beats.purpose: The telestrator circles the real detail (the turn).

devices.example: A keyboard launcher: "she's got four windows open and two seconds on the clock... the shortcut! Let's see that again: look at the fuzzy match on 'fgma'."
pitfalls: Noise: the telestrator must reveal a real detail
Stats must be real

build.note: Scoreboards, telestrator strokes, replay wipes over real UI.

devices.name: The Movie Trailer
devices.what: Epic trailer grammar: studio logos, "In a world...", a stinger.

beats.name: Stinger
beats.purpose: A last joke after the title.

devices.example: A to-do app: "In a world... where every list grows longer... one app... will say no." Title card, release date, stinger: an unchecked box twitches.
pitfalls: Heavily parodied; the most predictable parody there is
Needs specific wit or a structural twist

build.note: Type, whooshes, flashes, a date stinger.

devices.name: The Legal Disclaimer / Terms & Conditions
devices.what: The fine print starts telling the truth and slowly takes over the ad.

beats.name: The fine print tells the truth

devices.example: A privacy-first email app: "*We do not read your email. We could not if we tried. Side effects include an inbox that isn't a product."
pitfalls: Must stay legible
Best as a coda or a short

build.note: Scaling fine print, a calm plate behind it.

devices.name: The Horoscope / Fortune
devices.what: Readings by star sign or tarot card that are secretly use cases.

beats.name: Sign-by-sign readings
beats.purpose: Each a specific use case, escalating.

beats.name: The final card
beats.purpose: The turn: a reading for the viewer.

devices.example: A budgeting app: "Scorpio: you have 14 subscriptions and use two. Gemini: you split a dinner in 2022 and still think about it. Leo: this is the month you finally save."
pitfalls: List-shaped: needs escalation and a turn
Twelve signs is too many; three to five

build.note: Tarot-card frames, constellations drawn with strokes.

devices.name: The Obituary / Eulogy
devices.what: A mock-solemn farewell to the old way.
devices.example: A scheduling tool: "The Reply-All Thread, 1996-2026. It found a time for no one. It is survived by 41 'does Tuesday work?' messages."
pitfalls: Can feel negative; keep it light
Mocking something the audience still uses

build.note: A funeral program or memorial card, candlelight, a slow push.

devices.name: The Interface-as-World
devices.what: The camera travels through a landscape built from the product's UI: menus as architecture, notifications as weather.

beats.name: The edge of the world
beats.purpose: We arrive; the UI is terrain.

beats.name: Problem terrain
beats.purpose: A place that's broken or impassable.

beats.name: Overview
beats.purpose: Pull back: the whole world, ordered.

devices.example: A project tracker: a city of issue cards, a traffic jam of blocked tickets, and a new road of dependencies that clears it.
pitfalls: Very craft-heavy
Abstract without a protagonist

build.note: 2.5D layered UI planes are doable; full 3D is costly.

devices.name: The Oner
devices.what: No cuts: one continuous camera move connects every station of the story.

beats.name: Tight on a detail
beats.purpose: The first frame is a close-up of one thing.

beats.name: Stations
beats.purpose: Three or four stops, each joined by a match-point.

beats.name: The surprise station
beats.purpose: The turn: somewhere the viewer didn't expect.

beats.name: Wide on the lockup
beats.purpose: The whole path, ending on the name.

devices.example: A file-sharing app: follow one file from a designer's canvas, through a link, into a client's inbox, onto a printed poster on a wall.
pitfalls: Momentum must never drop
Transitions need clever match-points, not dissolves

build.note: A continuous canvas pan or zoom; the hero technique for HyperFrames.

devices.name: The Zoom from Cosmos to Cursor
devices.what: One continuous zoom across scales, from the universe to a single character (or back).

beats.name: A single pixel or character
beats.purpose: The payoff is the small end (the turn).

devices.example: A payments API: from orbit to one city, one cafe, one card tap, one cent landing in a ledger.
pitfalls: The glowing globe is the infra cliche
The payoff must be the small end, not the globe

build.note: Layered scale transforms; an infinite zoom is feasible in 2D.

devices.name: The Object's POV
devices.what: The story as lived by a thing the product touches.

beats.name: Birth
beats.purpose: The object comes into the world.

beats.name: Rescue
beats.purpose: The turn: the product finds it.

beats.name: Purpose fulfilled
beats.purpose: It becomes what it was meant to be.

devices.example: A photo-backup app: the life of one photo, taken at a wedding, buried in a camera roll of 40,000, nearly lost with a dropped phone, found and printed in an album.
pitfalls: Anthropomorphism turns saccharine
Hold one POV rule strictly

build.note: The object as a character in an illustrated world; small title cards ("Day 41").

devices.name: The Split-Screen Sync
devices.what: Two or more panels whose motions continue across the divide until they merge.

beats.name: First motion match
beats.purpose: An action continues across the divide.

beats.name: One frame
beats.purpose: The unified image and the name.

devices.example: A translation app: left a speaker in Tokyo, right a listener in Lagos; every gesture and word continues across the split until they share one frame.
pitfalls: Matches must be exact or it looks sloppy
Needs a reason for the two sides

build.note: Frame-exact sync is trivial in code; that's the advantage.

devices.name: The Static Camera, Changing World
devices.what: A locked-off frame; everything changes inside it over time.

beats.name: Calm again
beats.purpose: The frame at rest; the name.

devices.example: A home-energy app: a top-down view of one kitchen for a year; lights left on pile up as glowing dots until, one day, they start switching off by themselves.
pitfalls: Needs rhythm and one surprise or it's wallpaper

build.note: One composed frame with state changes over time.

devices.name: The Map / Journey
devices.what: A dotted line across a map tells the story and resolves into a shape.

beats.name: The route revealed
beats.purpose: The turn: zoomed out, the path is a shape or a word.

devices.example: A delivery app: one courier's day as a route line; zoom out and a week of routes draws the city's name.
pitfalls: The travel-line cliche
The reveal-shape must feel earned

build.note: SVG path draw, pins, a zoom-out.

devices.name: The Mirror / Symmetry
devices.what: The frame is split into mirror worlds (old and new, you and future you) that diverge and converge.

beats.name: The sides converge
beats.purpose: The turn: they meet again, or one crosses over.

devices.example: A language app: two identical travellers; one practices five minutes a day; by the last frame one orders dinner and the other points at the menu.
pitfalls: A before/after in disguise unless the visual rule is strict

build.note: A mirrored composition, one side's timeline offset.

devices.name: A Day in the Life at 100x
devices.what: A compressed day showing the product's effect in every micro-moment.
devices.example: A fitness tracker: a hyperlapse commute, lunch, stairs, slowing only on the moment the runner beats yesterday's time.
pitfalls: The number-one LLM default
Only with a strong twist: whose day? an object's? the least likely person's?

build.note: Speed ramps and time stamps.

devices.name: The Time-lapse of a Year
devices.what: Twelve months in thirty seconds, with one moment where time stops.
devices.example: A savings app: a year as a jar on a windowsill, seasons changing outside, coins arriving on every payday until December, when it tips into a plane ticket.
pitfalls: Samey without the one moment where time stops

build.note: A calendar flip, a chart that grows, seasonal color shifts.

devices.name: The Countdown
devices.what: Numbers ticking down structure the film, each number a beat.

beats.name: The first number
beats.purpose: Sets the clock and the stakes.

beats.name: The count breaks
beats.purpose: The turn: it stops early, jumps, or goes negative.

devices.example: A CI service: "minutes until the build finishes: 42... 41..." and at 38 it cuts straight to 0: "passed."
pitfalls: Predictable unless the count is subverted

build.note: Big numerals, a clock, hard cuts on each tick.

devices.name: The Reverse (rewind)
devices.what: The story runs backwards from the outcome to a surprising origin.

beats.name: The surprising origin
beats.purpose: The turn: the tiny first cause.

devices.example: A design tool: a finished billboard un-prints, layers un-stack, colors drain, back to one pencil line on a napkin.
pitfalls: Backwards motion must stay legible; use strong readable actions

build.note: In code you can literally reverse the timeline.

devices.name: The Loop That Tells a Story
devices.what: A seamless loop whose repetitions change a little each time until it breaks.
devices.example: A reminders app: the same morning repeats (alarm, keys, door, back for the forgotten thing) until one loop the phone buzzes first and the door closes for good.
pitfalls: Too subtle on first watch; make each variation obvious

build.note: One loop with per-iteration variables.

devices.name: Real Time
devices.what: The task happens uncut, in exactly the time it takes, with the timer on screen.

beats.name: Timer stops
beats.purpose: The number is the headline (the turn).

beats.name: What's left
beats.purpose: The time the viewer gets back.

devices.example: A site builder: 00:00, a sentence typed, a published page at 00:08.4. "The rest of this video is yours." Black.
pitfalls: Only works if the number is impressive and true

build.note: Real UI, a running timer, no cuts.

devices.name: The Letter from the Future
devices.what: Future-you writes to present-you about the moment things changed.

beats.name: The struggle, remembered
beats.purpose: Now seen from the other side.

devices.example: A language app: "Dear January-me, it's August. I just argued with a taxi driver in Italian and won. Do the five minutes."
pitfalls: Sentimental; needs a precise voice and specific details

build.note: Handwritten type on paper, small illustrated inserts.

devices.name: The Misdirect / Reveal
devices.what: The audience believes one thing; the turn reveals another and reframes everything.

beats.name: Confident setup
beats.purpose: A film that looks like one genre.

beats.name: The reveal
beats.purpose: The turn: it was something else.

devices.example: A password manager: a lush perfume-ad about "a name you whisper, a secret only you keep"; the reveal: it's someone typing their dog's name into a login for the ninth time.
pitfalls: The misdirect must be fair
The reveal must add meaning, not just a gotcha

build.note: A genre pastiche, then a hard switch of register.

devices.name: The List That Breaks
devices.what: A rhythmic list sets a pattern, then one item breaks it.

beats.name: The new list or the punchline

devices.example: An inbox app: "Archive. Reply. Archive. Reply. Archive. Reply. Archive... Lunch."
pitfalls: The break must be genuinely surprising and on-message

build.note: Cut to the beat; the break lands on a musical gap.

devices.name: The Rule of Three, Subverted
devices.what: Two setups and a twisted third.
devices.example: A photo editor: "Fix the sky. Fix the light. Fix... your uncle."
pitfalls: A known formula; the third must fit the product truth

build.note: Three matched shots.

devices.name: The "What It's Not" Montage
devices.what: The product is defined by rejecting the alternatives, one by one.

beats.name: It's not...
beats.purpose: Three to five rejections, each visualized.

beats.name: It's...
beats.purpose: The turn: the one true thing.

devices.example: A note app: "Not a second brain. Not a productivity system. Not a template marketplace. A blank page that opens in 80 ms."
pitfalls: Negative framing
Knocking named competitors can backfire

build.note: Crossed-out type, a hard cut to the true thing.

devices.name: The Mistake That's Corrected
devices.what: The film gets it wrong on purpose, then corrects itself on screen, more than once.

beats.name: Strike-through
beats.purpose: A red pen or a glitch.

devices.example: A grammar tool: "Write better emails" is struck to "write fewer emails", struck to "write the one email that gets a yes", circled.
pitfalls: Can look like a real error if under-designed

build.note: Strike-throughs as SVG strokes, editorial red.

devices.name: The Before / After Split
devices.what: A direct comparison: the old way, the new way, the delta.
devices.example: A spreadsheet tool: a 40-tab monster on the left, one clean view on the right.
pitfalls: The number-two LLM default and the heart of the cliche arc
Only with a structural twist (split-sync, mirror, rewind)

build.note: A wipe between two states.

devices.name: The Question Chain
devices.what: Every scene answers the last question and asks the next; the final answer is the product.

beats.name: Answer / next question
beats.purpose: Each answer opens the next door.

beats.name: The deep question
beats.purpose: The turn: the one nobody asks.

devices.example: A water-quality sensor: "Where does tap water come from?" "A reservoir." "Who checks it?" "Once a quarter, a lab." "And the other 89 days?"
pitfalls: Lecture-like; keep every answer visual

build.note: Each answer a diagram that becomes the next question's frame.

devices.name: A to Z
devices.what: An alphabetical sprint where each letter is a beat and Z is the punchline.

beats.name: The sprint
beats.purpose: Rhythm changes, a slowdown on one letter.

devices.example: A marketplace app: "A is for Avocado slicer. B is for Bike (used, one careful owner)..." to "Z is for Zero trips to the store."
pitfalls: Long; best as a 20-30 s speed format

build.note: Letter-by-letter cuts on the beat.

devices.name: The One Number
devices.what: A single real statistic, built, unpacked and made emotional.
devices.example: A security scanner: "212 days": the (sourced) average time to find a breach; each day a tile, then the tiles collapse to one.
pitfalls: A made-up stat kills trust: it must be sourced in the truth sheet

build.note: Count-ups, the number as particles or tiles.

devices.name: Escalation (and then...)
devices.what: Each beat raises the scale absurdly until it snaps back to something small.

beats.name: Back to small
beats.purpose: The turn: one crisp action collapses it.

devices.example: A photo cleaner: one blurry screenshot, a folder, a phone that won't boot, a landslide of duplicates down Main Street, one tap: 12 photos.
pitfalls: The snap back must be crisp

build.note: Scale tweens are cheap in code.

devices.name: Call and Response
devices.what: A rhythmic exchange between two voices, or text and image, accelerating to unison.
devices.example: A voice assistant: "Lights?" click. "Music?" a beat drops. "That thing I said I'd remember?" a reminder pops. Faster. "Done."
pitfalls: Monotony; vary the rhythm

build.note: Cut to music; each response a UI state.

devices.name: The Interrogation
devices.what: A tense Q&A (detective, auditor, courtroom) where the product is the alibi.
devices.example: An audit-log tool: under a swinging lamp, "who deleted the prod database?"; the log slides across the table: timestamp, user, rollback. "...Carry on."
pitfalls: Handle fear playfully, not threateningly

build.note: Noir illustration, hard light, the product's real record as evidence.

devices.name: The Product as a Character
devices.what: The product has a personality, a desire and a flaw.
devices.example: A sleep app as a grumpy nightlight that desperately wants its owner to put the phone down.
pitfalls: The friendly blob mascot is an LLM default
Needs a real personality flaw
Cheapens a serious product

build.note: Character animation; keep it to simple shape-based acting.

devices.name: The Problem as a Villain
devices.what: The problem is personified as a funny, specific villain.
devices.example: A spam filter: "The Prince", a velvet-robed schemer mailing inheritance offers, whose empire shrinks one blocked message at a time until he's just a guy with a laptop.
pitfalls: Cartoon-germ ad territory; keep the villain funny and specific

build.note: Shape-based character, props from the product's world.

devices.name: The Letter to Someone
devices.what: A narrator addresses one specific person, with shared history and a confession.
devices.example: A shared-calendar app: "Dear Mum, sorry about the missed call on your birthday. And the other one. From now on, you're in the calendar, not the backlog."
pitfalls: Saccharine; specific details save it

build.note: Type-driven, with small illustrated memories.

devices.name: The Documentary Interview / Mockumentary
devices.what: Talking heads recount a transformation, earnestly or deadpan.

beats.name: We tried everything
beats.purpose: The comedy of the old way.

devices.example: An invoicing tool: a three-person agency deadpans, "Our system was Priya remembering." Priya: "I was a good system."
pitfalls: Needs faces: render as illustrated heads or audio-led with type lower thirds

build.note: Illustrated interviews or audio with typographic lower thirds.

devices.name: The Inner Monologue
devices.what: A calm exterior, a frantic interior: the user's thoughts spiral over a mundane action.
devices.example: A travel-docs app at airport security: smiling outside; inside "passport? PASSPORT. Did I pack it. I touched it at 6 am. Did I put it back—" a tap. "...Lovely day."
pitfalls: Generic unless the thoughts are hyper-specific

build.note: Kinetic type as thoughts over a still or simple scene.

devices.name: The Founder Monologue
devices.what: The maker talks straight to camera with attitude, walking through the world.

beats.name: Why the old way is absurd

devices.example: A razor subscription: the founder walks a warehouse, one sight gag per sentence, ending on the URL.
pitfalls: Depends on charisma
Needs real footage; without it, a text-to-camera voice ("Hi. I'm the app.")

build.note: Pure code can only fake it as text-to-camera; buildable with supplied founder footage.

devices.name: The Skeptic Converted
devices.what: The whole film follows the one person who refuses the product.
devices.example: A shared-docs tool: the office's fax-machine loyalist watches the team co-edit all year; in December he quietly asks, "...how do I share this?"
pitfalls: The skeptic must be lovable, not a straw man

build.note: Character animation across a few set pieces.

devices.name: The Unexpected Protagonist
devices.what: The story is told from the least likely participant's side: the accountant, the dog, the pen.

beats.name: X's world
beats.purpose: Who we're following, and why they're unlikely.

beats.name: X's relief
beats.purpose: The turn: the product changes their day.

devices.example: A pet-care app told by the dog: every day at 5 pm the walk doesn't happen; then a buzz, a reminder, and the leash comes down.
pitfalls: Keep the product visible through the side character's eyes

build.note: Character-led illustration, POV framing.

devices.name: The Single Extended Metaphor
devices.what: One metaphor rendered physically and pushed as far as it will go.
devices.example: Noise-cancelling headphones: the city's noise is physical debris flying at a commuter; with the headphones on, it freezes mid-air and she walks through it.
pitfalls: Mixed metaphors
A hostile second reading: ask what else it could mean

build.note: Depends on the metaphor; favor ones built from shapes and type.

devices.name: The Chain Reaction
devices.what: A Rube Goldberg machine where each link is a real step of the product.

beats.name: The chain
beats.purpose: Each link is a real feature or step.

beats.name: Near-failure
beats.purpose: The turn: a link stalls; suspense.

devices.example: An integration platform: a form submission tips a marble through a CRM funnel, a Slack bell rings, an invoice slides out of a slot.
pitfalls: Too long
Every link must map to a real step

build.note: GSAP-choreographed physics along a continuous pan; true physics needs care.

devices.name: The Game Level
devices.what: The task as a specific video game: HUD, levels, a boss.

beats.name: The boss
beats.purpose: The turn: the product is the power-up.

devices.example: A focus app as a block-stacking game: notifications fall faster and faster until focus mode clears four lines at once.
pitfalls: Generic retro pixels are overused: pick one specific game grammar

build.note: Sprites, a HUD, a score counter.

devices.name: The Miniature / Diorama World
devices.what: Everything built at tiny scale: tiny workers act out the story until a giant hand intervenes.

beats.name: Tiny people act out the story

devices.example: A warehouse-inventory app: tiny workers in a cardboard city hunt for one missing box; a giant phone light sweeps over and the shelves reorder themselves.
pitfalls: Expensive for real; in code stylize as paper-craft 2.5D

build.note: Paper-craft 2.5D with tilt-shift blur.

devices.name: The Graphic System
devices.what: A strict visual rule is the idea: one color, one shape, one icon, repeated with variations.

beats.name: Variations
beats.purpose: The rule applied in surprising places.

beats.name: The lockup
beats.purpose: The same end card every time.

devices.example: A messaging app: black frames, white shapes, and the brand's one accent color appears only when a message is delivered.
pitfalls: Weak without a very strong, simple rule

build.note: The ideal code-built format.

devices.name: The Cover Version of a Famous Ad
devices.what: A shot-for-shot homage of a known ad or scene, with one substitution that makes the point.
devices.example: A version-control tool remakes a famous manifesto ad: "Here's to the ones who commit often..." over portraits of history's great note-keepers.
pitfalls: Legal / IP risk
Parody without insight is noise; needs a real reason to cover that ad

build.note: Recreate the source's type and rhythm, not its footage.

devices.name: The Material Study
devices.what: A product quality expressed as the behavior of an abstract material.
devices.example: A database: tangled threads (queries) knot and snap; the new engine pulls them into one taut, humming strand.
pitfalls: Abstract, so it needs a clear rule to read

build.note: Shape physics, springs, morphs: the ideal code-built format.

devices.name: The Parable / Fable
devices.what: A short moral tale in a timeless world.
devices.example: A meditation app: "Once, a monkey lived in a busy temple, jumping from bell to bell..."
pitfalls: Slow; keep it under 60 s for a launch

build.note: Cut-paper or woodcut illustration, slow parallax.

devices.name: The 5-Second Film
devices.what: An entire concept in five seconds: one image, one turn, the name.
devices.example: A battery-saver app: a phone at 1%; a tap; it's 1% for the rest of the day (time-lapse clock). Name.
pitfalls: Needs a context or a distribution hook

build.note: One composed shot.

devices.name: The Typographic Manifesto
devices.what: Only words, set with intention, carry a belief.

beats.name: Provocation
beats.purpose: The first line picks a fight.

devices.example: A code editor: "Every tab is a thought you haven't finished. / Every setting is a decision you shouldn't have to make. / We removed 214 of them."
pitfalls: Platitudes: every line must be concrete and specific

build.note: The core HyperFrames strength.

devices.name: Made-With / Proof-as-Film
devices.what: The film is made from the product's own output or data; its existence is the proof.

beats.name: The reveal of the source
beats.purpose: The turn: it was all made with the product.

devices.example: A charting library: a 30-second film whose every frame is a chart rendered live by the library, ending "every frame: 14 lines of code."
pitfalls: Privacy when using user data
The output must be beautiful
Must genuinely be the product's output

build.note: Data-viz is native to code; needs the real output or data.

devices.name: The Data Letter
devices.what: Oddly specific aggregate usage facts, delivered as direct address.

beats.name: Escalating letters
beats.purpose: Three to five, stranger each time.

devices.example: A recipe app: "Dear the 3,112 people who searched 'pasta but fancy' at 11 pm: we see you."
pitfalls: Needs real data (sourced in the truth sheet) and respect for privacy

build.note: Billboard-style type cards.

devices.name: The One-Word / One-Color / One-Shape Film
devices.what: A self-imposed constraint the whole film respects, broken once at the climax.
devices.example: A sound app built only from its waveform line: a skyline, a heartbeat, a mountain range, a flat line (the break: silence), then the logo.
pitfalls: Too clever; the break must mean something

build.note: One SVG element morphing: ideal for code.

devices.name: The Sound-First Film
devices.what: The soundtrack is built from the product's own sounds; the picture follows the sound.
devices.example: A mechanical keyboard: key clicks become the hi-hat, the spacebar the kick, and every cut is locked to them.
pitfalls: Needs strong sound design and real product sounds

build.note: Depends on audio assets; picture cuts locked to the sound.

devices.name: The Fake UI Takeover
devices.what: The video pretends to be the viewer's own screen or feed until the product breaks the fourth wall.

beats.name: It looks like the platform
beats.purpose: A familiar UI (a feed, an ad, a desktop).

beats.name: The product appears in the UI
beats.purpose: It acts on the fake screen.

devices.example: An ad blocker as a pre-roll: the "Skip Ad" button is replaced by the product's icon, which eats the ad you're watching.
pitfalls: Platform-specific
Can annoy
Don't imitate a platform's UI so closely it misleads

build.note: A fake platform UI, a cursor, one interaction.

devices.name: A Different Medium Every Beat
devices.what: Each beat is one short task drawn in a completely different art medium; one fixed home look holds the film together between them, and the jolt of every switch is the beat.

beats.name: Home look
beats.purpose: The fixed frame the film returns to: a stage, a counter, a score.

beats.name: Command and medium 1
beats.purpose: One word, one action, one result, in the first medium.

beats.name: Command and medium 2..n
beats.purpose: A new medium each time; the hero keeps two or three silhouette marks.

beats.name: The failure
beats.purpose: One funny miss that the viewer can read at once.

beats.name: The product's medium
beats.purpose: The last beat is the product's own look, held longer.

devices.example: A tax app: file a receipt in crayon, sort a drawer in ink wash, catch a deadline in pixels, then the clean real screen for the refund.
pitfalls: A style sampler with no rule: every beat needs a stake and a result grasped in a second
The home look must come back between beats or the film falls apart
Every medium is a simplified redrawing; one channel trick each (pressure, wetness, a grid), not a filter

build.note: One small renderer per medium on a shared timeline; the home stage stays DOM.

devices.name: Five Things Accelerating
devices.what: The film speeds up on a plan: at each step tempo, how long a scene lasts, how long a title is held, how long the command is shown and the characters' frame rate all tighten together.

beats.name: Slow and legible
beats.purpose: The rule is taught at the calmest speed.

beats.name: First step up
beats.purpose: All five variables tighten at once; the viewer feels it.

beats.name: Second step up
beats.purpose: Faster again; a rising run in the score marks each step.

beats.name: Last life
beats.purpose: The groove drops to a heartbeat just before the final speed.

beats.name: Release
beats.purpose: The product slows everything back to a calm, held frame.

devices.example: A scheduling tool: bookings arrive every 4 s, then 3, then 2, then 1, the cuts and the labels shrinking with them, until it clears the whole day and the frame goes still.
pitfalls: Changing only the tempo: it must be five things together or it reads as a speed-up filter
A failure at top speed goes unread: make the action overshoot and hit something, or replay it
Over 60 s the frenzy wears out

build.note: One tempo table (step -> beat length, scene length, dwell, hold, fps) drives every timing.

devices.name: One Line, One Hidden Picture
devices.what: A single continuous line draws a chain of small vignettes; a final pull-back shows they were all part of one big picture the whole time.

beats.name: The line starts
beats.purpose: One stroke, a small drawing, a first small joke.

beats.name: Chapters
beats.purpose: Each vignette morphs into the next; the line never leaves the paper.

beats.name: The pull-back
beats.purpose: The camera retreats across scales and the vignettes become parts of one picture.

beats.name: The picture is the answer
beats.purpose: What it spells is the point: a skyline, a map, the mark.

devices.example: A coffee roaster: a bean, a cup, a hand, a street, a window, until the pull-back shows the whole line was the outline of one giant cup.
pitfalls: Stray connectors read as wrinkles and beards: plan the path like an Euler path, where a closed motif is a circuit that ends where it began, and fix the topology rather than the drawing
Test the whole path at final scale after every change
Each chapter must hold its own joke or the line is just a line

build.note: SVG paths sampled by arc length, joined by tangent-continuous connectors; time assigned by curvature; a camera that follows the nib.

devices.name: Ghosts of the Old Lesson
devices.what: A faint trace of an earlier drawing, answer or draft stays on the surface, and the turn is that it becomes relevant: the old thing was nearly right, or exactly wrong.

beats.name: A board with ghosts
beats.purpose: Faint marks of an old explanation are already there, unnoticed.

beats.name: The new lesson
beats.purpose: A clean new drawing goes over and between them.

beats.name: The ghost lines up
beats.purpose: One old mark meets one new mark; the old way is the problem, or the origin.

beats.name: The erase
beats.purpose: The old is wiped but a trace always remains.

devices.example: A new forecasting model: last year's chart is a pale ghost on the board; the new curve is drawn over it and the two split exactly where the old assumption broke.
pitfalls: Ghosts that are decoration: one must come back and matter
Too bright: ghosts live at 5 to 10% ink
An eraser that removes a label you needed

build.note: A hand-lettered surface with a stored layer of faint old strokes, a camera that travels across it, an eraser band at about 90% strength so a ghost remains.
